column1: # The forms of expression the slot matrix puts into an operand position (@PLN221).
#   type  what the expression gives; a slot takes the fillers of its own type
#   expression  `<C>` is the counter the cell hands this operand.  Every filler but a type's
#         `var` bumps that counter exactly ONCE per evaluation, and gives the same value as
#         the `var` of its type, so a cell and its bound-first twin agree on the answer.
#   A filler that bumps `calls` itself and writes no log (`int-block-one`: a block of ONE
#   statement and a value, which is lowered differently from a longer one) gets no ORDER cell.
#   A filler is a primary expression or stands in parentheses, so that the statement around
#   it parses the same way as with a variable there.
#   `<I:type>` in an expression is a HOLE: the row is a WRAPPER, generated once for every
#   other filler of that type (never a variable, never another wrapper) at `--depth 2`.  A
#   wrapper takes no `<C>` — the filler in its hole does the counting — and gives its own
#   type's plain value when its hole holds that type's plain value.
#   An optional fourth column, `first`, marks a filler that WRITES what the statement works
#   on.  Such an operand changes the answer, so only the bound-first twin can say what is
#   right, and only where binding first is what the rules say: the slots whose count is
#   `first` (scripts/syntax_slots.tsv).  A row with this column goes into those slots only.
# The `var` row of a type is its plain operand: evaluated once by construction, it is what a
# slot is validated with before any other filler is tried.
# `python3 scripts/slot_matrix.py check` validates this file; `fillers` runs each row.
